variations.name: Heavy-duty electric trucks, semis & electric freight services
variations.description: Battery-electric Class 8 tractors and rigid trucks (plus freight-as-a-service operators that sell electric trucking capacity) replace diesel in regional haul, drayage and increasingly long-haul — the single largest diesel fuel pool in road freight.

companies.name: BYD
companies.what: Vertically integrated (cells-to-vehicle) Chinese giant selling 8TT/Q1 Class 8 tractors and a full e-truck range in China, North American ports and Latin America.
companies.signal: China accounts for the vast majority of global e-truck sales; BYD among top sellers with global plants

companies.name: Volvo Trucks
companies.what: Broadest western heavy BEV lineup (FH/FM/FMX/VNR Electric); new FH Aero Electric does 700 km per charge; long-time EU/NA electric HDT share leader.
companies.signal: Thousands of heavy e-trucks delivered across ~50 markets since 2019; led EU share until Mercedes overtook in 2025

companies.name: Daimler Truck
companies.what: eActros 600 long-hauler (500+ km, megawatt-charging-ready) in Europe and Freightliner eCascadia in US drayage/regional haul.
companies.signal: Became the EU's largest zero-emission heavy truck seller in 2025 (~1,400 units; ~5% of its EU sales by Q4)

companies.name: Tesla
companies.what: Semi Class 8 tractor with ~500-mile range; dedicated factory at Giga Nevada reached high-volume production in 2026 after PepsiCo and other fleet pilots.
companies.signal: 965 of 1,067 California voucher requests in the Dec 2025 window were for Tesla Semis; volume production started 2026

companies.name: Traton (Scania / MAN)
companies.what: Series-production 40-44t BEV tractors (Scania battery-electric R/S, MAN eTGX) built on main European lines since 2024-25.
companies.signal: MAN began series eTGX production in 2025; Scania scaling BEV output at Södertälje

companies.name: Windrose Technology
companies.what: Belgium-headquartered, China-engineered aerodynamic long-haul e-tractor (670 km at 49t GCW, 800V); US assembly via partner Xos.
companies.signal: $110M Series B (2025, HSBC/HITE) plus ~$100M strategic; targeting NYC IPO mid-2026 and first US deliveries 2025-26

companies.name: Einride
companies.what: Swedish electric freight-as-a-service operator (sells freight capacity, not trucks) with driver-operated e-fleets plus cab-less autonomous pods for Amazon, AB InBev and others.
companies.signal: Completed $1.35B SPAC merger and began Nasdaq trading June 10, 2026 (ENRD); shares rose ~74% on debut

companies.name: WattEV
companies.what: Trucks-as-a-service drayage carrier pairing its own Class 8 BEV fleet with public megawatt charging plazas (incl. solar-powered Bakersfield depot) in California.
companies.signal: ~$109M in federal/state grants for charging corridor build-out; dozens of electric trucks in revenue service

companies.name: Nikola
companies.what: BEV/FCEV Class 8 pioneer that delivered a few hundred trucks; filed Chapter 11 in February 2025 after cash burn and recalls.
companies.signal: Lucid bought its Arizona factory and HQ lease for ~$30M at the April 2025 bankruptcy auction; truck business not continued

companies.name: Volta Trucks
companies.what: Purpose-built 16t urban Volta Zero with central driving position; first bankruptcy Oct 2023 after battery supplier Proterra's collapse, relaunched under Luxor Capital, then failed again.
companies.signal: Second insolvency announced May 2025 after an investor pulled out; staff unpaid for 8 weeks; liquidation likely

variations.name: Medium-duty & vocational trucks (incl. refuse and utility)
variations.description: Class 4-7 box trucks, step-van chassis, refuse and utility trucks have predictable depot-based routes that suit batteries, making them the most economically rational early segment for fleet electrification.

companies.name: Harbinger
companies.what: Purpose-built Class 4-6 strip chassis with in-house 800V powertrain priced near diesel; also a hybrid-electric RV chassis line.
companies.signal: $100M Series B (Jan 2025); serial production started Apr 2025; 4,690-vehicle order book worth ~$500M

companies.name: Xos
companies.what: Nasdaq-listed step-van/stripped-chassis OEM for parcel and uniform fleets (FedEx Ground, UPS, Cintas), plus mobile charging units; US assembly partner for Windrose semis.
companies.signal: 1,000+ vehicles delivered cumulatively; 328 units in 2025

companies.name: Battle Motors
companies.what: Successor to Crane Carrier building EV (and diesel) cabover refuse and vocational trucks with in-house LFP packs in Ohio.
companies.signal: Raised $150M+ (Series B, 2023); EV refuse trucks deployed with US municipal fleets

companies.name: Mack Trucks (Volvo Group)
companies.what: LR Electric Class 8 refuse chassis purpose-built for curbside collection, paired with McNeilus/Heil bodies.
companies.signal: First major-OEM electric refuse truck in North America; in service with NYC DSNY, Republic Services and others

companies.name: Daimler Truck (Fuso / Rizon)
companies.what: Fuso eCanter light-medium cabover sold in 40+ markets since 2017 (3rd generation), plus the Rizon brand of Class 4-5 e-trucks for North America.
companies.signal: Thousands of eCanters in service globally; Rizon launched in the US in 2023

companies.name: Isuzu
companies.what: NRR-EV Class 5 cabover with modular battery options — the electric version of America's best-selling low-cab-forward work truck.
companies.signal: Production launched 2024 for US fleets

companies.name: Oshkosh Corporation
companies.what: Fully integrated electric vocational vehicles: McNeilus Volterra ZSL/ZFL refuse trucks, Pierce Volterra fire apparatus, and USPS Next Generation BEV mail trucks.
companies.signal: Volterra ZFL front-loader debuted at CES 2025; USPS BEV deliveries ramping

companies.name: Bollinger Motors
companies.what: Class 4 B4 cab-forward electric chassis (production launched Sept 2024 under Mullen Automotive ownership).
companies.signal: Receivership Mar-Jun 2025, shut down Nov 2025, second receivership Dec 2025; assets and remaining trucks auctioned May 2026

companies.name: Tevva
companies.what: UK maker of 7.5t battery-electric trucks (with hydrogen range-extender variants) supplied to Royal Mail and Travis Perkins.
companies.signal: Entered administration June 2024 after a failed merger with ElectraMeccanica; production ceased

variations.name: Electric delivery & step vans
variations.description: Purpose-built electric cargo vans and step vans serve last-mile parcel and trade fleets where stop-start urban duty cycles maximize the efficiency and brake-regen advantages of EVs.

companies.name: Rivian
companies.what: Purpose-built EDV/RCV delivery vans co-designed with Amazon, now also sold to non-Amazon fleets.
companies.signal: Amazon's Rivian fleet grew 50% in 2025 to 30,000+ vans in the US; 100,000-van target by 2030

companies.name: Ford Pro
companies.what: E-Transit — the best-selling electric cargo van in the US and a leader in Europe, bundled with Ford Pro charging and telematics.
companies.signal: Tens of thousands delivered since 2022; US e-van segment leader

companies.name: Mercedes-Benz Vans
companies.what: eSprinter and eVito built on dedicated lines in Germany/US; major supplier to Amazon's European electric fleet.
companies.signal: Amazon's EU fleet topped 10,000 e-vans in 2025, with ~5,000 Mercedes vans added that year

companies.name: GM BrightDrop
companies.what: Purpose-built Zevo 400/600 vans from CAMI, Ontario; GM ended production in Oct 2025 citing weak demand after US incentives were eliminated (GM itself continues, the van line is dead).
companies.signal: Q3 2025 sales of 2,384 (+869% YoY) still not enough; line discontinued with no relocation

companies.name: Flexis
companies.what: Software-defined 800V electric van family (Step-in, Cargo, Panel) for urban logistics, founded as Renault-Volvo-CMA CGM JV; Renault moved to take 100% ownership in Feb 2026.
companies.signal: €350M+ invested; serial production starts at Renault Sandouville in 2026

companies.name: Farizon (Geely)
companies.what: Geely's new-energy commercial vehicle arm; drive-by-wire SV electric supervan exporting to Europe and Asia-Pacific.
companies.signal: SV shortlisted for International Van of the Year 2026; European launch 2025

companies.name: Workhorse
companies.what: W56 Class 5/6 electric step vans built in Union City, Indiana (5,000+/yr single-shift capacity); consolidated the US step-van EV niche by merging with Motiv in Dec 2025.
companies.signal: Post-merger cost reductions enabled price cuts up to $61,000 per van in 2026 to spur demand

companies.name: Motiv Electric Trucks
companies.what: EPIC chassis and Argo step-van electrification pioneer with hundreds of vehicles at fleets like Bimbo Bakeries and Purolator.
companies.signal: Merged into Workhorse in December 2025

companies.name: Arrival
companies.what: UK 'microfactory' electric van startup once valued at $13B via SPAC with a 10,000-van UPS order.
companies.signal: Entered UK administration Feb 2024; assets sold off piecemeal

companies.name: Canoo
companies.what: Skateboard-platform LDV/LV electric delivery vans, including a USPS pilot and NASA crew transport vehicles.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 7 liquidation January 2025

variations.name: Transit buses & coaches
variations.description: Battery-electric city buses are the most mature heavy EV segment — fixed routes, depot charging and high diesel displacement per vehicle made them cost-competitive on TCO first, with China's fleet already majority electric and EU new sales approaching half zero-emission.

companies.name: BYD
companies.what: World's most prolific e-bus maker with tens of thousands delivered (Shenzhen's 16,000-bus fleet onward) and assembly plants on three continents.
companies.signal: ~80,000+ e-buses delivered globally since 2011

companies.name: Yutong
companies.what: World's largest bus manufacturer; dominant in Chinese e-buses and the top exporter to Latin America, Central Asia and Europe.
companies.signal: ~190,000 new-energy buses delivered cumulatively (company figure)

companies.name: New Flyer (NFI Group)
companies.what: North America's largest transit bus maker; Xcelsior CHARGE NG battery buses and MCI electric coaches.
companies.signal: Record orders/backlog in 2024-25 as US transit agencies electrify

companies.name: GILLIG
companies.what: Private US transit bus builder with a growing battery-electric line; bought Lightning eMotors' Colorado assets (2024) to in-source EV powertrain work.
companies.signal: Hundreds of BEBs delivered to US agencies

companies.name: Solaris (CAF)
companies.what: Polish-built Urbino Electric family; perennial #1 or #2 in European zero-emission city bus deliveries.
companies.signal: Thousands of e-buses in 30+ countries; ~20% EU ZE-bus share

companies.name: Ebusco
companies.what: Dutch maker of lightweight composite-body e-buses (Ebusco 3.0); serial liquidity crises since 2024 despite restructuring.
companies.signal: Workforce halved to 282 FTE in 2025; €32M debt restructured; exploring sale of controlling stake in bus division (Apr 2026)

companies.name: Wrightbus
companies.what: Northern Irish builder of electric (and hydrogen) double-deckers; revived after 2019 administration by Jo Bamford and growing rapidly in UK/EU/APAC.
companies.signal: Record order intake 2024-25; one of UK's fastest-growing manufacturers

companies.name: Olectra Greentech
companies.what: India's largest electric bus maker (BYD-licensed technology) supplying state transport undertakings under FAME/PM-eBus Sewa schemes.
companies.signal: Thousands of e-buses delivered or on order across Indian cities

companies.name: Proterra
companies.what: US e-bus and battery pioneer that filed Chapter 11 in Aug 2023; transit bus business sold to Phoenix Motor, battery business to Volvo.
companies.signal: Cautionary tale: ~$1B+ raised, 1,000+ buses delivered, still failed on cost/contracts

companies.name: Van Hool
companies.what: 124-year-old Belgian bus and coach maker (incl. CX45E electric coaches for North America) that went bankrupt April 2024; VDL bought the bus/coach operations.
companies.signal: One of Europe's largest coach makers; collapse shifted EU e-coach work to VDL/Schmitz

variations.name: Electric school buses
variations.description: Electric school buses pair short, predictable routes with long midday/overnight dwell times — ideal for charging and V2G — and remove diesel exhaust from children's commutes; US adoption is driven by the EPA Clean School Bus Program and state subsidies.

companies.name: Blue Bird
companies.what: Only US pure-play school bus OEM (publicly listed); its EV line is profitable and built in Georgia.
companies.signal: Record 901 electric buses delivered in FY2025 (of 9,409 total); record $221M adj. EBITDA

companies.name: Thomas Built Buses (Daimler Truck)
companies.what: Saf-T-Liner C2 'Jouley' Type C electric bus using Accelera (ex-Proterra) powertrains.
companies.signal: 1,500+ electric buses delivered across North America

companies.name: IC Bus (Navistar/Traton)
companies.what: Electric CE Series school bus plus new full-service zero-emission contracts (charging + uptime).
companies.signal: ~1,500 electric school buses on the road

companies.name: Micro Bird
companies.what: Blue Bird-Girardin JV building the G5e Type A (small) electric school bus in Quebec.
companies.signal: Leading Type A electric supplier in US/Canada

companies.name: LION (ex-Lion Electric)
companies.what: Former North American e-school-bus volume leader (~2,500 delivered); collapsed under CCAA in Dec 2024 and was sold for C$6M to a Quebec investor group in May 2025, restarting as a Quebec-only school bus maker.
companies.signal: US plants and truck lines abandoned; ~1,000 buses kept running in Quebec backed by ~$500M provincial subsidy renewal

companies.name: GreenPower Motor
companies.what: Purpose-built BEAST Type D and Nano BEAST Type A electric school buses assembled in West Virginia and California.
companies.signal: Laid off workers and paused WV production May 2025 citing tariffs; small volumes and weak balance sheet

companies.name: Highland Electric Fleets
companies.what: Electrification-as-a-service: owns buses/chargers and sells districts a per-mile contract including V2G revenue and maintenance.
companies.signal: $253M Series B (2023); 1,000+ buses under contract across 30+ states/provinces

companies.name: Zum
companies.what: Tech-enabled student transportation operator converting district fleets to electric with V2G (delivered Oakland USD, the first major-district 100% electric fleet, 2024).
companies.signal: ~$140M Series E (2024) at ~$1.3B valuation; multi-district CA/CO contracts

variations.name: Construction & compact equipment
variations.description: Battery-electric excavators, loaders and compact machines eliminate diesel use and noise on jobsites; China's electric wheel loaders crossed 25% monthly sales penetration in 2025 while western OEMs commercialize compact and mid-size machines for urban/indoor work.

companies.name: XCMG
companies.what: Largest electric construction equipment range (33 BEV loader models plus excavators, mixers, dump trucks); #1 in China's booming electric loader market.
companies.signal: China electric loader penetration hit 26.6% in July 2025 (16,344 units Jan-Jul, +154% YoY); XCMG market leader

companies.name: SANY
companies.what: 21+ electric models across loaders, excavators, mixer trucks and dump trucks with in-house battery integration.
companies.signal: Top-3 in Chinese zero-emission construction machinery output

companies.name: LiuGong
companies.what: Neck-and-neck with XCMG in battery-electric loaders (the two hold ~50% of China BEV loader production); exporting 856H-E MAX loaders globally.
companies.signal: ~Half of China's BEV loader output together with XCMG

companies.name: Volvo CE
companies.what: Broadest western electric lineup from 2.5t compact machines to the 23t EC230 Electric excavator and L120 Electric loader.
companies.signal: EC230 Electric commercially available in North America early 2025; L120 Electric deliveries from 2026

companies.name: Komatsu
companies.what: PC210E 20t lithium-ion electric excavator (Europe/Japan) plus electric minis and compact models.
companies.signal: First major Japanese OEM with a 20t-class production electric excavator (2023-24)

companies.name: Bobcat (Doosan)
companies.what: T7X/S7X all-electric compact track and skid-steer loaders that replace hydraulics entirely with electric actuation, plus electric mini-excavators.
companies.signal: T7X launched 2022 with Sunbelt Rentals placement; S7X following

companies.name: Caterpillar
companies.what: Battery-electric prototypes across four machine families with battery production in-house; reportedly acquired collapsed Monarch Tractor's electric/autonomy technology in 2026.
companies.signal: Demonstration-stage machines at customer sites; cautious commercial rollout

companies.name: Wacker Neuson
companies.what: 'Zero emission' compact line — electric mini-excavators, wheel loaders, dumpers and rammers — widely sold for EU urban and indoor jobsites.
companies.signal: One of the largest zero-emission compact portfolios in Europe

companies.name: Firstgreen Industries
companies.what: Czech manufacturer of fully electric skid-steer loaders (ROCKEAT, MiniZ) sold into European and US niche/indoor markets.
companies.signal: Niche exporter; one of few pure-play electric earthmoving startups

variations.name: Mining trucks & underground equipment
variations.description: Battery-electric haul trucks and underground loaders/drills cut diesel (a top-2 mine operating cost), eliminate ventilation-driven energy demand underground, and are moving from underground commercial fleets to first ultraclass surface deployments.

companies.name: Epiroc
companies.what: Underground BEV pioneer (battery loaders, 42t Minetruck, drill rigs) with batteries-as-a-service financing model.
companies.signal: Hundreds of battery units delivered; repeat full-fleet orders in Canada and Australia since 2021

companies.name: Sandvik
companies.what: Underground BEV leader via its Artisan acquisition; TH665B 65t battery truck and LH518iB loader.
companies.signal: Largest-ever BEV order (~SEK 750M) from South32's Hermosa project booked Q2 2025; repeat Eldorado Gold orders Q3/Q4 2025

companies.name: Liebherr
companies.what: T 264 240t battery-electric haul trucks (3.2 MWh pack) with 6 MW DC fast chargers, built around Fortescue Zero power systems; ~360-truck autonomous fleet for Fortescue.
companies.signal: US$2.8B partnership (Sept 2024) — the largest zero-emission mining equipment order to date; first truck fitted out May 2026

companies.name: Fortescue Zero
companies.what: Mining major's own OEM arm building battery power systems, MW-class fast chargers and electric drivetrains for its 'Real Zero 2030' diesel exit.
companies.signal: Electrifying ~$400M/yr of diesel spend; first 6 MW charger deployed 2026

companies.name: XCMG Mining
companies.what: Chinese OEM contracted to supply up to half of Fortescue's next 300-400 zero-emission 240t haul trucks — first ultraclass BEV export deal from China.
companies.signal: Up to 400-truck agreement (Sept 2025); deliveries 2028-2030

companies.name: Caterpillar
companies.what: 793 battery-electric 'early learner' ultraclass trucks in trials with BHP, Rio Tinto and Teck, plus the R1700 XE underground battery loader and dynamic/trolley charging concepts.
companies.signal: Multi-site early-learner program 2024-26; commercial launch staged

companies.name: Komatsu
companies.what: 'Power-agnostic' 930E-class haul truck platform (battery, trolley, future H2) unveiled at MINExpo 2024 plus underground battery equipment.
companies.signal: Demonstrators with anchor customers; full launch later this decade

companies.name: MEDATech
companies.what: Canadian engineering firm whose ALTDRIVE battery conversions electrify Western Star haul/utility trucks and drills for mines, with MW charging.
companies.signal: Multiple mine-site BEV deployments in Canada

companies.name: MacLean Engineering
companies.what: Underground support vehicles (bolters, graders, boom trucks) offered as a full EV Series line.
companies.signal: Fleet has accumulated millions of electric operating kilometres at customer mines

companies.name: First Mode
companies.what: Anglo American-backed developer of hybrid hydrogen-battery retrofits for ultraclass haul trucks (nuGen).
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 Dec 2024 after Anglo pulled funding; Cummins acquired assets and IP Feb 2025

variations.name: Agricultural tractors & farm equipment
variations.description: Battery-electric tractors replace diesel in compact and specialty farm work (orchards, vineyards, dairy, municipal), where fixed depots and shorter duty cycles fit current battery energy density; large row-crop horsepower remains out of reach.

companies.name: Monarch Tractor
companies.what: MK-V 70hp driver-optional electric tractor (Foxconn-built) targeting vineyards and dairies; raised ~$240M including a $133M Series C (2024).
companies.signal: Warned of shutdown and filed WARN layoffs Nov 2025; wound down by early 2026; tech reportedly sold to Caterpillar Apr 2026

companies.name: Solectrac
companies.what: California compact electric tractors (e25, e70N) for vineyards and small farms.
companies.signal: Parent Ideanomics filed Chapter 11 Dec 2024; Solectrac assets sold to Tillou Management; operations minimal

companies.name: AGCO / Fendt
companies.what: e107 Vario 75-90hp battery tractor — the first full-size production e-tractor from a major, aimed at specialty/municipal users.
companies.signal: On sale in UK/EU (~£200k list); narrow-track e107 V variant for vineyards

companies.name: John Deere
companies.what: 130hp E-Power utility tractor (built on acquired Kreisel battery tech) plus electric compact equipment and a battery backhoe.
companies.signal: Early customer production units in 2026; commercial production to follow

companies.name: Kubota
companies.what: Compact electric tractors (LXe-261) and utility vehicles offered via leases in Japan and pilots in Europe.
companies.signal: Cautious staged rollout in compact segment

companies.name: New Holland (CNH)
companies.what: T4 Electric Power — 75hp utility e-tractor with autonomy features, developed initially with Monarch technology.
companies.signal: Limited production for North American specialty/utility customers since 2024

companies.name: Sonalika
companies.what: Tiger Electric — low-cost compact e-tractor sold in India since 2020 for smallholder and haulage duty.
companies.signal: One of the only e-tractors selling in a volume emerging market

variations.white_space: Field agriculture is brutally hard for batteries (multi-day harvest peaks at 200+ hp, remote fields, thin dealer/service networks), and the VC route just failed publicly — Monarch and Solectrac both collapsed despite ~$300M combined raised — leaving incumbents to stage 75-130hp launches. The opening is depot-based specialty fleets (orchard, vineyard, dairy, municipal) with swappable packs, autonomy-bundled TCO, and low-cost compacts for India/Africa rather than head-on row-crop competition.

variations.name: Port/terminal tractors, airport GSE & material handling
variations.description: Yard/terminal tractors, airport ground support equipment and forklifts run short repetitive cycles near fixed power — electric forklifts are already the mature majority of sales, and electric terminal tractors/GSE are the fastest-scaling beachhead for Class 8-weight EVs.

companies.name: Orange EV
companies.what: US pure-play electric terminal truck OEM selling turnkey trucks-plus-charging; claims the largest deployed heavy-duty EV base in the country.
companies.signal: 1,600+ trucks across 300+ fleets in 40 states; fleet passed 10 million operating hours Oct 2025

companies.name: Kalmar
companies.what: Ottawa T2E+ electric terminal tractors plus electric reachstackers, straddle carriers and forklifts for ports.
companies.signal: Largest western port-equipment maker; fully-electric portfolio target

companies.name: Terberg
companies.what: Dutch family-owned yard tractor leader; YT203-EV electric terminal tractors at DCs and ports across Europe and North America.
companies.signal: Electric YT in serial production since 2020

companies.name: Toyota Material Handling
companies.what: World's #1 forklift maker; the majority of counterbalance/warehouse trucks it sells are already electric, increasingly lithium-ion.
companies.signal: Electric is the mature default in Class 1-3 material handling globally

companies.name: Jungheinrich
companies.what: German intralogistics pure-play; ~98% of trucks sold are electric and it pioneered factory-fit li-ion forklifts.
companies.signal: One of the top-3 global forklift makers, effectively 100% electric

companies.name: Hyster-Yale
companies.what: Electric 'big trucks' — laden container handlers, reachstackers and terminal tractors for ports (alongside hydrogen options).
companies.signal: Electric laden container handler pilots at LA/Long Beach

companies.name: ITW GSE
companies.what: Electric ground power units (eGPU) and point-of-use power replacing diesel GPUs at airport gates worldwide.
companies.signal: Battery eGPU 7400 deployed at major hubs

companies.name: TLD Group
companies.what: World's largest GSE maker with a full electric line — baggage tractors, belt loaders, pushbacks (e-GSE).
companies.signal: e-GSE now a large share of new orders as airlines decarbonize ground ops

companies.name: Mototok
companies.what: German remote-controlled electric aircraft pushback tugs that remove diesel tractors from the gate.
companies.signal: Adopted at scale by Lufthansa, British Airways and others

companies.name: Gaussin
companies.what: French electric/hydrogen terminal tractor and airport logistics vehicle maker (ATM, AGVs) once slated to supply Amazon-bound trucks.
companies.signal: Judicial liquidation Nov 2024 with ~€140M debt after failed 355-vehicle North American contract; takeover bids rejected

variations.name: Truck & bus repower/retrofit conversions
variations.description: Converting existing diesel trucks and buses to battery-electric drive reuses the chassis (cutting cost and embodied carbon) and can electrify fleets faster than new-build supply — but certification costs and falling new-EV prices have bankrupted most players.

companies.name: pepper motion
companies.what: German retrofit kits ('etrofit') converting Mercedes buses and trucks to electric; pivoted to technology supplier before failing.
companies.signal: Insolvent Feb 2024; bought by a Turkish investor, then folded into Haller Group alongside Quantron with a 2026 relaunch

companies.name: Lightning eMotors
companies.what: Colorado electrifier of Class 3-7 shuttles, school buses and Ford/GM chassis (~600 vehicles deployed).
companies.signal: Ceased operations Dec 2023 after NYSE delisting; GILLIG bought the assets in 2024

companies.name: SEA Electric
companies.what: SEA-Drive electric drive systems fitted to new glider truck chassis (Hino partnership) across Australia, NZ and the US.
companies.signal: Acquired by Exro Technologies in Feb 2024 amid financial strain

companies.name: Evolectric
companies.what: California 'CircularEV' kits converting used Class 4-8 diesel trucks, targeting US fleets and Latin American markets where new BEVs are unaffordable.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; pilot fleets in US and emerging markets

companies.name: BEDEO
companies.what: UK/Turkish van electrifier (owns Protean in-wheel motors) converting Stellantis large vans to electric or range-extended 'reborn electric' drive.
companies.signal: Thousands of van conversions delivered to EU fleets and post services

companies.name: UEV (ex-Lunaz Applied Technologies)
companies.what: Upcycles diesel refuse trucks into remanufactured EVs at Silverstone (David Beckham-backed Lunaz brand).
companies.signal: Entered administration 2024; relaunched as 'Upcycled Electric Vehicle' after restructuring — viability unproven

companies.name: Magtec
companies.what: Sheffield-based veteran repower house converting refuse trucks and specialist vehicles for UK councils and defence.
companies.signal: Decades of drive system deployments; UK council refuse EV conversions

companies.name: Janus Electric
companies.what: Australian conversions of Class 8 prime movers to electric with 4-minute swappable batteries and its own charge-and-change station network.
companies.signal: ASX-listed May 2025 (A$8.8M raise); 23 trucks converted, 155 confirmed orders, 9 swap stations

variations.white_space: The graveyard here (pepper, Lightning eMotors, Lunaz, SEA, e-troFit) shows the economics: one-off engineering and certification on aging chassis can't beat falling new-BEV prices in rich markets. The credible openings are standardized kits for captive high-utilization fleets whose chassis outlive powertrains (refuse, terminal tractors, transit buses), retrofit-friendly regulatory regimes (France's décret rétrofit, India), and battery-swap conversions like Janus where charging infrastructure is the binding constraint.

variations.name: Electrified trailers & range-extending add-ons
variations.description: Powered e-axles, battery dollies and electric trailer hubs add traction or power to the trailer itself, cutting a diesel tractor's fuel 20-40% or extending a BEV tractor's range — electrifying freight without replacing the truck.

companies.name: Range Energy
companies.what: Powered eTrailer with a force-sensing smart kingpin that assists any tractor — no truck modification — cutting fuel use roughly a third.
companies.signal: $31.5M raised (incl. $23.5M round Feb 2024 with Yamaha, UP.Partners); fleet pilots moving to production

companies.name: Revoy
companies.what: Swappable-battery 'EV dolly' inserted between tractor and trailer with corridor swap stations, sold per-mile so diesel trucks run as near-EVs on set lanes.
companies.signal: Venture-backed; commercial corridor service live in the US South-Central since 2024

companies.name: ConMet eMobility
companies.what: PreSet Plus eHub in-wheel motors on trailer axles that regenerate braking energy to power electric refrigeration units (TRUs).
companies.signal: Commercial pilots with major reefer fleets

companies.name: ZF
companies.what: Trailer e-axles (AxTrax LF) and eTrailer systems supplied to trailer OEMs for recuperation and traction assist.
companies.signal: Tier-1 scale supplier bringing trailer electrification to series production

variations.white_space: Very few credible players because powered trailers sit in a regulatory grey zone (weight allowances, braking rules) and the industry splits incentives — tractor owners buy fuel while trailer owners buy trailers. An opening exists for per-mile leased range-extension that leaves the tractor and its warranty untouched, bridging fleets to electrification years before Class 8 BEVs and megawatt charging are ubiquitous.

variations.name: Battery-swap heavy trucks & swap ecosystems
variations.description: Heavy trucks with standardized swappable packs decouple the battery from the vehicle purchase and refuel in ~5 minutes, which is why roughly a third of China's surging electric heavy-truck sales are swap-capable — the fastest route to diesel parity in 24/7 freight.

companies.name: CATL (Qiji Energy)
companies.what: Built the #75 standardized swappable heavy-truck pack and a national swap-station network, including a 1,250 km Chengdu-Shanghai corridor opened Dec 2025.
companies.signal: Stations compatible with 95% of mainstream Chinese HDT models; 300-station target; CEO projects 50% HDT electrification by 2028

companies.name: SPIC (Qiyuan)
companies.what: State Power Investment Corp arm that pioneered battery-as-a-service financing and operates one of China's largest swap-truck/station fleets.
companies.signal: Battery-swap models were ~32% of China's Q1 2025 new-energy heavy truck sales

companies.name: XCMG
companies.what: Among the top sellers of new-energy heavy trucks in China, including swap-capable tractors for mines, ports and steel logistics.
companies.signal: China NEV heavy truck sales hit ~25% penetration mid-2025 and >30% by Nov 2025 (28,000 units that month)

companies.name: SANY
companies.what: Leading electric heavy truck OEM offering both charge and swap variants plus its own swap stations.
companies.signal: Consistently top-3 in China NEV HDT sales

companies.name: FAW Jiefang
companies.what: China's biggest truck maker; J6-based swap-capable e-tractors integrated with the Qiji standardized-pack ecosystem.
companies.signal: Among a dozen OEMs with 30+ truck models compatible with CATL's 75# pack

variations.white_space: Outside China this approach is nearly empty (Australia's Janus Electric is the lone notable player) because swap needs pack standardization across OEMs — a chicken-and-egg no western truck maker will start. The opening is corridor consortia (drayage lanes, mining/port shuttles) adopting a standard pack with battery-as-a-service financing, potentially importing CATL's proven 75# model.
